## `lakana login`

Usage: `lakana login [OPTIONS]`

Verify a credential and save it as a profile.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--profile` | text | none | Profile name to write. |
| `--url` | text | none | Platform URL. |
| `--token-stdin` | flag | off | Read the token from stdin (for CI). |
| `--env` | text | none | Default environment. |

## `lakana logout`

Usage: `lakana logout [OPTIONS]`

Remove a saved profile (and its token) from the profile file.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--profile` | text | none | Profile to remove. |

## `lakana whoami`

Usage: `lakana whoami [OPTIONS]`

Show who the configured credential authenticates as.

## `lakana load`

Usage: `lakana load [OPTIONS] {file} {table}`

Load FILE into TABLE of the bronze layer, once.

Shows the schema and the row count and asks before it writes. A first load creates the table; later loads replace its rows or, with --write append, add to them, and fail clearly if someone changed the table in between. For anything that should run again, write a Python asset instead.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FILE` | path | required | The local file: CSV, Parquet, Arrow, JSON, NDJSON or a spreadsheet. |
| `TABLE` | text | required | The bronze table; a bare name means bronze.<name>. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--write` | text | `replace` | replace (the default) or append, once the table exists; a first load creates it. |
| `--format` | text | none | The file's format, if the extension doesn't say. |
| `--sheet` | text | none | A spreadsheet's sheet (default: the first). |
| `--header-row` | whole number | `1` | Row of the column names in a CSV or sheet; 0 for none. |
| `--yes` | flag | off | Don't ask for confirmation. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

## `lakana sql`

Usage: `lakana sql [OPTIONS] {query}`

Run SQL and print (or save) the result, or write it into a table.

With `--into T --mode create --expire-after N` the new table expires N days after its last write or read.

A query that stays queued for 3 seconds prints a line on standard error that says why ('Waiting: ...'), and again when the reason changes; the result still goes to standard output only. Nothing is printed about waiting with --output json.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QUERY` | text | required | The SQL, or - to read it from stdin. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--out` | path | none | Write the full result to this file. |
| `--format` | text | none | parquet, csv, arrow or xlsx (default: from the extension). |
| `--max-rows` | whole number, 0 or more | `50` | Most rows to display. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait before giving up. |
| `--into` | text | none | Write the result into this table or view instead of printing it. |
| `--mode` | text | none | create, replace, append or view (needs --into). |
| `--incremental-key` | text | none | Append only rows past the target's max of this column. |
| `--evolve-schema` | flag | off | Let the target adopt the result's schema. |
| `--expire-after` | whole number, 1 to 3650 | none | Let the new table expire this many days after its last write or read. |
| `--break-glass` | flag | off | Write to a protected environment outside a run (needs MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT; audited). |
| `--reason` | text | none | Why, 10-500 characters on one line (with --break-glass). |

## `lakana configuration`

Usage: `lakana configuration [OPTIONS]`

Show the running server's configuration (admin only).

One row per setting with its environment variable, its value and whether the server's environment set it (`set`) or it is the default. A secret shows only `(secret, set)` or `(secret, not set)`, never its value. Needs the ADMIN role.

## `lakana deploy`

Usage: `lakana deploy [OPTIONS] [repo]`

Deploy REPO to an environment; exit 1 if the deploy fails.

In a CI job, LAKANA_OIDC=github or LAKANA_OIDC=gitlab (or LAKANA_OIDC_TOKEN) exchanges the job's OIDC ID token for a one-deploy CI token instead of reading a stored token.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPO` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--ref` | text | none | Branch, tag or full SHA. |
| `--dry-run` | flag | off | Validate and diff only. |
| `--no-wait` | flag | off | Print the deploy id and exit. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait. |

## `lakana orphans`

Usage: `lakana orphans [OPTIONS]`

List tables earlier project versions produced that no current one does.

One page at a time; the last line names the command for the next page when there is one. A dropped table that can still be restored is listed as ``dropped, restorable``.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 200 | none | Most rows to list (default 100). |
| `--cursor` | text | none | Continue after the page that printed this cursor. |

## `lakana run`

Usage: `lakana run [OPTIONS] [repo]`

Run REPO's deployed project version; exit 0 on success, 1 otherwise, 7 if one is active.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REPO` | text | none | Repository name (default: lakana.yaml's repo:). |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |
| `--select` | text, repeatable | none | Asset pattern (shell glob); repeatable. |
| `--upstream` | flag | off | Add every ancestor. |
| `--downstream` | flag | off | Add every descendant. |
| `--no-wait` | flag | off | Print the run id and exit. |
| `--timeout` | number | none | Seconds to wait. |

## `lakana status`

Usage: `lakana status [OPTIONS]`

Show whether the instance is healthy, degraded or down, and why.

Prints one line: Healthy, Degraded or Down, and a sentence that says why. An administrator (who may manage environments on the instance) also sees the busy task slots, the workers' memory against their limits, and the workers as lakana worker list shows them. Degraded means work gets done, slower or at risk; Down means nothing gets done.

Exit code: 0 for Healthy and for Degraded, 12 for Down (also with --output json), so a script can branch on it. While the catalog database is down the command cannot check who you are and fails with the server's error (exit code 11); the address /readyz still answers then.

## `lakana search`

Usage: `lakana search [OPTIONS] {TEXT}`

Find tables, columns, labels, descriptions, runs, people and glossary terms that match TEXT.

Matching ignores case and finds TEXT anywhere in a name, label or description. Exact matches come first, then names and labels that start with TEXT, then those that contain it, then descriptions. Texts in a table's main language always match; translated ones in your language (--lang, else your profile's, else the instance's main language), and the matched column shows a translation's language in brackets. A table or column is listed once. Runs are found by the first four or more characters of their id, their job or their repository. A table is also found by the grain its asset header declares, and shows its kind in brackets after its name; a column by the label or description of its declared measure. Glossary terms are found by their name, synonyms and definition; a table or column a term links is found by the term's name and synonyms, and shows `term` and that term's key in the matched column. You see only what you may read. Use --output json for every field.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | text | required | What to find; 1 to 200 characters. |
| `--kind` | one of `table`, `column`, `run`, `principal`, `term` | none | Only this kind of result. |
| `--model-kind` | one of `fact`, `dimension`, `wide`, `staging` | none | Only tables whose asset header declares this kind; other results are left out. |
| `--limit` | whole number, 1 to 100 | `20` | Most results to show (1 to 100). |
| `--offset` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Results to skip, to show the next page. |
| `--lang` | text | none | Match translated labels and descriptions in this language, such as de or fr-CH. |
| `--env` | text | none | Environment (default: the profile's). |

## `lakana init`

Usage: `lakana init [OPTIONS] [directory]`

Create a Lakana project that deploys unchanged.

Nothing is overwritten: if a file it would write exists, or a folder inside the project is a symbolic link (a write through it could land outside the project), it writes nothing.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DIRECTORY` | path | `.` | Project directory (default: here). |
| `--repo` | text | none | Repository name (default: the directory name). |
| `--sample` / `--no-sample` | flag | none | Write a small sample to build and query (default: yes for a local instance). |
| `--ci-auth` | one of `oidc`, `pat` | `oidc` | How the CI files sign in: oidc exchanges the CI job's ID token, so nothing secret is stored in CI; pat reads a stored Lakana token. |
| `--template` | one of `python`, `ingest-files`, `ingest-sql`, `ingest-rest`, `medallion` | none | Start from a template. python: the sample plus one Python asset, locked with `uv lock` (needs network access and a few more minutes). ingest-files, ingest-sql or ingest-rest: one asset that ingests from a source, instead of the sample. medallion: a bronze, silver and gold star schema with generated retail data, layer rules, German translations and a glossary (no source needed). |
